KEY MESSAGE 1...Light rain will continue to impact Delmarva and
far southern New Jersey through this morning.

High pressure well to the north continues to push its influence
southward across the area. However, there remains broad
diffluence aloft that is sufficient to keep a band of light rain
extending into Delmarva and southern New Jersey. The upper
forcing for ascent looks to wane by dawn, and thus the band of
rain should dissipate by 9-10 AM.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A strengthening surface low off the Eastern 
Seaboard will keep persistent northeast to north flow in place 
through at least Friday. Depending on the track of the low, it 
could bring increased rainfall chances and windy conditions to 
the parts of the region Friday and into the weekend.

A mid-level trough currently traversing portions of the Midwest
into the Ohio Valley will continue eastward and amplify towards
the Eastern Seaboard today. Weak surface cyclogenesis has begun
off the coast of the Carolinas, with the low expected to 
continue intensifying through late this week. The initial track 
of the developing low is expected to be to the northeast, well 
offshore. However, with a strong high centered over portions of 
Quebec, a sharp pressure gradient over the region will at least 
lead to breezy conditions through Thursday. The strongest 
pressure gradient, and thus winds, are forecast to occur on 
today into tonight. It should remain mostly dry today (following
the early morning light rain) through Thursday.

Given a consistent forecast for sustained northeast winds 25-35
mph along the Atlantic coasts of New Jersey and Delaware today,
the Wind Advisory remains in effect for the immediate coastal 
strip. This was extended in time through 8 PM Thursday evening, 
mainly due to the forecast for sustained winds continuing into 
Thursday. Some gusts near 45-50 mph are also possible.

For late this week into this weekend, model guidance remains 
largely split into two camps. One camp allows the low to 
continue to track northeastward away from the region, and the 
other camp features a westward deviation of the low, or even 
additional surface cyclogenesis closer to the coast. Given these
factors, uncertainty for Friday and beyond remains quite high, 
with a large range of potential outcomes. The deterministic EC 
and all of its ensembles continue to feature the scenario that 
would lead to greater impacts. The deterministic GFS remains far
enough out to sea to keep impacts confined to the immediate 
coast with gusty winds and minimal rainfall. The 00Z
deterministic GFS and EC runs were both slower in the low
pressure strengthening and a bit farther east again, which does
seem to be a more probable solution given upper level wind field
evolution. Nevertheless, uncertainty for forecast details Friday
and beyond remains high. With that said, regardless of the
exact outcome, coastal flooding, marine and surf hazards are 
expected to continue through at least Saturday.

PoPs increased some in the eastern half of our area, and are now 
in the 20-60% range into the weekend. Regardless of which 
scenario pans out, precipitation chances and winds will be 
highest close to the coast and decrease with inland extent.

Sunday night into Monday, regardless of which scenario 
ultimately pans out, the low will begin to track away from the 
area, allowing rain chances to decrease and winds to subside. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Multiple rounds of significant tidal flooding 
expected for this week. Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories 
are in effect.

With a slow moving coastal storm and multiple days of strong
northeast winds expected, the confidence in the threat for 
tidal flooding remains high. Strong onshore flow that is 
projected to last for several days will result in water piling 
up across tidal tributaries and within back bays of coastal 
communities. Tidal levels will also be enhanced with 
astronomical tides increasing with the upcoming Full Moon on 
Saturday. This combination of factors will lead to widespread 
tidal flooding, some of which is expected to get to the Moderate
stage. While not currently forecast, the threat for major 
flooding is not off the table, especially getting near the full 
moon. Tidal guidance diverges greatly beyond Thursday Night at 
nearly all of our forecast points. Some guidance has moderate to
even major flooding for the weekend while some barely has tide 
levels getting into minor flood stage. It all will depend on the
track of the coastal storm. 

Most areas within the Coastal Flood Advisory saw widespread 
minor flooding on Tuesday, especially back bay communities. The
forecast remains on track. The Coastal Flood Warnings and 
Advisories for Delaware and Salem County are already in effect. 
Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories go into effect this 
afternoon for the NJ Atlantic coastline. These were extended in
time to cover the high tides through Friday evening. While the
